title: The party ({présenter}, {chanter}, {danser}, {détester})
description: It is Léa's birthday party. Introduce your friends, say who sings and who dances, and say what you love or hate doing: {Je te présente Maya. Hugo chante, mais je déteste danser.}
can_do: Introduce a friend to a friend with {je te présente}, and to an adult with {je vous présente}
Say who sings and who dances at a party
Say what you love or hate doing: {J'adore chanter, mais je déteste danser.}

vocabulary.note: A regular -er verb: {je présente}, {tu présentes}, {nous présentons}.
vocabulary.example_fr: Hugo, je te présente Maya, ma voisine.
vocabulary.example_en: Hugo, this is Maya, my neighbour.

vocabulary.example_fr: Hugo chante très mal, mais il adore ça.
vocabulary.example_en: Hugo sings very badly, but he loves it.

vocabulary.example_fr: Hugo chante et Maya danse avec Noé.
vocabulary.example_en: Hugo sings and Maya dances with Noé.

vocabulary.note: Like {aimer}, it takes a noun or an infinitive: {je déteste danser}.
vocabulary.example_fr: Je déteste danser, mais j'adore chanter.
vocabulary.example_en: I hate dancing, but I love singing.

vocabulary.note: Friends often start a sentence with it to give their real opinion.
{fière} for a girl or a woman: {Léa est fière de son frère.}
vocabulary.example_fr: Noé danse avec Maya, et il est très fier.
vocabulary.example_en: Noé is dancing with Maya, and he is very proud.

concepts.definition: To a friend, say {je te présente} and the person's name. To an adult you call {vous}, say {je vous présente}.
concepts.example: {Hugo, je te présente Maya.} (Hugo, this is Maya.) {Madame Garnier, je vous présente Maya.} (Mrs Garnier, this is Maya.)

concepts.term: Saying what you love or hate doing
concepts.definition: Put the infinitive straight after {aimer}, {adorer} or {détester}, with nothing between them.
concepts.example: {J'adore chanter, mais je déteste danser.} (I love singing, but I hate dancing.)

phrases.fr: Hugo est un copain, et Maya est une copine.
Mon voisin chante, ma voisine danse.
Hugo chante, mais je déteste danser.

items.situation: The guests are arriving at Léa's flat for her birthday. Maya, who has just moved in upstairs, knows nobody. Introduce her to Hugo, Léa's best friend.

mistakes.feedback: Say who meets her: {je te présente Maya}.

mistakes.answer: Hugo, je te présente à Maya
mistakes.feedback: {je te présente à Maya} introduces Hugo to Maya. Put Maya straight after the verb: {je te présente Maya}.

items.situation: Mme Garnier comes up from the ground floor with a present for Léa: {Je passe juste dire bonjour !} She is 78, and everyone calls her {vous}. Introduce Maya to her.
items.answer: Madame Garnier, je vous présente Maya

mistakes.answer: Madame Garnier, je te présente Maya
mistakes.feedback: You call Mme Garnier {vous}: {je vous présente Maya}.

items.text: Maya, je te présente Noé, le frère ___ je t'ai parlé.
items.gloss: Maya, this is Noé, the brother I told you about.

mistakes.feedback: You say {parler de} someone, so the {de} becomes {dont}: {le frère dont je t'ai parlé}.

items.instruction: Maya has just moved from Montréal. Say the opposite with {ne … personne}.
items.shown: Maya connaît tout le monde ici.

mistakes.answer: Maya ne connaît pas personne ici
mistakes.feedback: {personne} takes the place of {pas}: {ne connaît personne}.

items.situation: Hugo is at the door. Ask him if he is singing tonight.
accept: est-ce que tu chantes ce soir ?

items.text: Hugo ___ très mal, mais il adore ça.
items.gloss: Hugo sings very badly, but he loves it.

mistakes.feedback: With {il} or a name, the ending is a silent -e: {Hugo chante}.
Conjugate the verb after {Hugo}: {Hugo chante}.

items.question: Hugo sings badly and loves it. Which line is his?

items.text: Hugo chante, et maman ___ dans la cuisine !
items.gloss: Hugo sings, and Mum dances in the kitchen!

mistakes.feedback: Maman is one person: {maman danse}.
Conjugate the verb after {maman}: {maman danse}.

items.instruction: Léa tells Maya what she and Hugo do at every party. Say it with {nous}.

mistakes.feedback: After {nous}, an -er verb ends in -ons: {nous dansons}, {nous chantons}.
After {nous}, an -er verb ends in -ons: {nous dansons}, {nous chantons}.

items.text: Maya ne veut pas danser. Hugo : Si tu danses, je ___ !
items.gloss: Maya doesn't want to dance. Hugo: If you dance, I'll sing!

mistakes.feedback: Conjugate the verb after {je}: {je chante}.

items.situation: Hugo wants you to dance: {Allez, essaie !} Tell him you hate dancing, but you love singing.
items.answer: je déteste danser, mais j'adore chanter
accept: je déteste danser, mais j'aime chanter
non, je déteste danser, mais j'adore chanter

mistakes.answer: je déteste de danser, mais j'adore de chanter
mistakes.feedback: Put the infinitive straight after the verb: {je déteste danser}, {j'adore chanter}.

mistakes.answer: je déteste danse, mais j'adore chante
mistakes.feedback: After {détester} and {adorer}, use the infinitive: {danser}, {chanter}.

items.text: Maya : T'as une belle voix, Hugo ! Hugo : ___, non ! Je chante très mal. Allez, on danse ?
items.gloss: Maya: You have a lovely voice, Hugo! Hugo: Honestly, no! I sing really badly. Come on, shall we dance?

mistakes.feedback: Keep the e in the middle: {franchement}.

items.question: Noé shouts {T'as vu ? Hugo danse !} Which words does {t'as} stand for?

items.instruction: Léa points at Hugo and tells Maya this. What does she mean?

items.text: Hugo veut chanter pour Léa. Je doute qu'il ___ bien !
items.gloss: Hugo wants to sing for Léa. I doubt he sings well!

mistakes.feedback: After {je doute que}, the verb takes the subjunctive. For {il}, it is {chante}.

items.text: Il y a des gens ___ chez Léa : il n'y a plus de place pour danser !
items.gloss: There are people everywhere at Léa's: there's no more room to dance!

mistakes.feedback: {nulle part} means nowhere. Here the flat is full: {partout}.

items.situation: Hugo puts on the same song for the third time. Ask your friends if you can change the music.
accept: est-ce qu'on peut changer de musique ?

items.text: Hugo va chanter pour Léa ? Ça va ___ drôle !
items.gloss: Hugo is going to sing for Léa? This is going to get funny!

items.text: Le gâteau arrive, avec du chocolat dessus. Tout le monde chante pour Léa, et Maya danse avec Noé. Noé est très ___ !
items.gloss: The cake arrives, with chocolate on top. Everyone sings for Léa, and Maya dances with Noé. Noé is very proud!

mistakes.feedback: Noé is a boy: {fier}. {fière} is for a girl or a woman.

items.situation: Everyone has sung {Joyeux anniversaire} to Léa, and Maya is dancing with Noé. Tell Noé, frankly, that he dances really well. Say it the way friends talk.
accept: Noé, franchement, tu danses trop bien !
franchement, Noé, tu danses trop bien !

mistakes.feedback: With {tu}, the -er verb adds a silent -s: {tu danses}.
{dansez} goes with {vous}. With {tu}, say {tu danses}.
